court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
trial_court: Family Court No.3, Nagpur in petition No.A-263/2007
case_name: Dr. Rajasi @ Swapna W/O Shashank Dandge vs Dr. Shashank S/O Vitthalrao Dandge

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Dr. Rajasi @ Swapna W/O Shashank Dandge (wife)

facts_of_case: The parties are doctors who got married in 2006. The wife went to her maiden home after some clashes during their honeymoon and the husband found abnormal traits in her behavior. She tried to commit suicide twice and was sent back to her home. The husband lodged a report with the police and she was not allowed to come back.

legal_principles.principle: A period of nearly five years having passed after filing the petition, the provision not entertaining the petition within one year is not mandatory.
legal_principles.held: The learned Judge has rightly held that ...

legal_principles.principle: A separation of more than 4½ years when the Judge, Family Court decided the matter is a vital aspect in marriage.
legal_principles.held: Therefore, the findings are not erroneous.

outcome.final_order: The trial court's order of dissolution of marriage on the ground of cruelty is upheld.

keywords: Latin maxim: 'actus curiae neminem esse judicium'
